source.title: Expand-and-Cluster: Exact Parameter Recovery of Neural Networks
source.authors: Flavio Martinelli; Berfin Şimşek; W. Gerstner; Johanni Brea

record.file_problem: none; the supplied text includes the paper and appendix.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether student width affects gradient-based convergence in teacher-student networks, using synthetic regression tasks and teacher-logit imitation rather than the claim versions’ specified classification-error tests.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own training results on synthetic teacher-student regression tasks. It also reports reconstruction results on MNIST and CIFAR10, but those measure parameter recovery or imitation loss, not the training classification error named by V1. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Figure A.9 reports the study's own width comparison for two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks on MNIST logits, bearing on V2 in a new setting. The recorded synthetic experiments use an asymmetric softplus-plus-sigmoid activation, and R4 concerns tanh; those rows do not test the ReLU-specific version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures a secondary optimization finding but omits the main conclusion: expanding students, clustering shared weight vectors and fine-tuning can recover teacher widths and parameters up to activation symmetries. Direct same-size training usually fails to recover them. Expansion improves synthetic convergence, with greater difficulty at larger r/din; demonstrated recovery remains limited to small-scale setups and substantial computation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses teacher-query regression and teacher-logit imitation, with synthetic gradient-flow experiments and Adam-trained students; it does not use the classification-error recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Overparameterization factor and teacher complexity r/din change convergence; the paper also reports a tanh exception in its MNIST imitation experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Asymmetric-activation synthetic students benefit from expansion: the equal-budget comparison succeeds in 2/1024 same-width runs versus 72/128 eightfold-width runs, with stronger difficulty at larger r/din.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Extra student width improves convergence in asymmetric-activation teacher-student regression, with the required width and training time depending on teacher complexity.

fits_no_version.finding: Expansion followed by clustering and fine-tuning recovers a teacher-sized network at machine-precision loss where direct same-width training fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Expansion, clustering and fine-tuning can recover teacher parameters more successfully than direct training at teacher width.

fits_no_version.finding: Tanh is a qualitative exception to the high-loss trapping of same-width MNIST students.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of expansion for teacher-logit imitation depends on the activation function.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning; Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The central width results are on synthetic regression or teacher-logit imitation, not training classification error. Some conditions are described qualitatively rather than with exact per-condition counts. Difficult synthetic tasks may not have converged within the allocated time.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each din and r combination in Figure 4: the supplied text gives overall trends but not the individual plotted values. MNIST and CIFAR10 reconstruction losses are omitted because they concern recovery or imitation performance rather than the training classification error in the versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error of large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and recipe-dependent exceptions.

The joint teacher/student size trend, widths 6–20, and the effect of adding exactly one or two neurons. The MNIST comparison does not quantify spurious-minimum frequencies or establish stationary endpoints.
Depth degradation in plain convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts or alternative training recipes.
Comparative effects of initialization on training speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth, curvature evolution and divergence.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and the Fixup comparison.

missing.what: A direct ReLU width-comparison row from Figure A.9: MNIST teacher width 64, same-width students versus width-256 students, measuring imitation RMSE before clustering. The caption reports high-loss trapping without expansion and lower losses with expansion; exact plotted values are not readable from the supplied text. Reconstruction outcomes should be recorded separately.
missing.locator: Figure A.9, ReLU panel and caption; Table 1; Appendix A.6.3

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for V2. The asymmetric-activation difficulty results and tanh exception do not justify limits_scope verdicts on the ReLU-specific version.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted or random labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, or regularization on that error.
The specific trend that spurious-minimum frequency rises as teacher and student grow together, and the stated 6-to-20-neuron range and one- or two-neuron excess comparison.
Depth effects in plain versus residual convolutional networks, and the cited initialization or normalization alternatives.
Comparisons of activation-matched initializations, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and training of very deep plain networks.
Training behavior at learning rates above a stability threshold, curvature or sharpness changes, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training without normalization.

rows.subject: student networks
rows.size_stated: teacher hidden-layer size r = 4; input dimensionality din = 4; students have 4, 8, 16 or 32 hidden neurons
rows.operation_detail: Trained students on teacher-generated data; compared direct training at teacher width with overparameterized training followed by Expand-and-Cluster reconstruction.
rows.measure: Convergence to zero or near-zero imitation loss
rows.baseline: 20 same-width students; none reached zero loss
rows.value: For the same teacher, Expand-and-Cluster with overparameterisation ρ ≥ 2 reconstructs the network up to machine-error zero loss.
rows.note: The reported zero-loss result is for the reconstructed network after training overparameterized students and applying Expand-and-Cluster; it is not a direct comparison of unmodified student endpoints alone.
rows.check: The activation is softplus(x) + sigmoid(4x), not ReLU. The machine-precision result also follows clustering and additional optimization, so it cannot establish that extra width alone removes spurious gradient-descent endpoints.

rows.subject: student networks
rows.size_stated: teacher din = 16, r = 4; students with ρ = 1 or ρ = 8
rows.operation_detail: Compared training success for same-size and overparameterized students under equal computational budget.
rows.measure: Successful training runs retrieving an identical input-output mapping
rows.note: The paper describes a significant improvement in success rate with the larger students.
rows.check: The counts are correctly reported, but this synthetic experiment uses the asymmetric activation rather than ReLU. Synthetic training also includes second-order optimization after gradient flow.

rows.subject: student networks
rows.operation_detail: Varied overparameterization and teacher complexity; trained multiple students for each synthetic teacher.
rows.baseline: Student networks of the same size as the teacher (ρ = 1) often get stuck in local minima.
rows.value: The text reports that ρ ≥ 2 students are more likely to converge to near-zero loss; for difficult teachers with r/din ≥ 1, training is very slow and convergence is not guaranteed in a reasonable amount of time.
rows.note: The paper gives qualitative trends here rather than per-condition counts in the supplied text. It states that the benefit weakens as r/din increases.
rows.check: The width and difficulty trends concern asymmetric-activation networks, outside V2. Difficult runs are explicitly unfinished, so their remaining loss cannot establish convergence to spurious local minima.

rows.subject: student networks
rows.size_stated: single-hidden-layer students imitating MNIST teachers of sizes 10, 30 or 60 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Compared students trained without overparameterization with overparameterized students across activation functions.
rows.value: The paper says tanh seems to be an exception to the pattern that same-size students get stuck at high loss; overparameterization is described as necessary to reliably reach lower losses overall.
rows.note: The result is qualitative in the supplied text, and the tanh exception qualifies the width effect.
rows.check: Tanh is outside V2's ReLU condition. Figure A.9 instead shows a tanh teacher of width 128 and students of width 128 or 512; the recorded sizes 10, 30 and 60 come from other appendix experiments.

relationships.condition: MNIST teacher-logit imitation with a shallow ReLU teacher of width 64 and students of width 64 versus 256
relationships.reason: Based on text rather than recorded rows: Figure A.9 reports high-loss trapping without expansion and lower imitation losses with fourfold width; ReLU is included, while only tanh is identified as an exception.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing student width from 64 to 256 reduced imitation losses relative to high-loss trapping without expansion.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Synthetic teacher-student regression tasks, particularly the din = 16, r = 4 equal-budget comparison
reader_labels.reason: Larger students had substantially more successful exact mapping runs than same-width students (R1, R2). This supports the extra-width convergence effect in the tested settings.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across the synthetic task family and MNIST teacher-logit imitation
reader_labels.reason: The width benefit weakens as teacher complexity r/din increases, convergence may remain slow or unguaranteed for difficult teachers, and tanh is reported as an exception (R3, R4).
